title: On maximal ladders
summary: Given a positive integer $n$, an $n$-ladder is a lower finite lattice whose elements have at most $n$ lower covers. In 1984, Ditor proved that every $n$-ladder has cardinality at most $\aleph_{n-1}$ and asked whether this bound is sharp, i.e., whether for each $n$ there is an $n$-ladder of cardinality $\aleph_{n-1}$. We isolate the notion of maximal $n$-ladder and use it to study Ditor's problem and related questions. We show that $\text{Add}(ω, ω_ω)$ forces every maximal $n$-ladder to have cardinality $\aleph_{n-1}$, and hence forces a positive answer to Ditor's question for every $n$. In…
